context: Tests whether the agent applies the-mister planning rules when writing an approved plan.md for a Go web service feature: git work isolated in Git-tier nodes, including questions that need git implicitly; tiers that follow the skill's tiering rule rather than a fixed expectation; the required inspections planned with an inspector that receives no implementer material; a Log that holds no fabricated state at approval; protected-path digests and a baseline test run before any build work; real paths in owns; and every command naming its directory.

checklist.name: Git-tier for all git work
checklist.description: Every node that runs git, gh or glab is Git-tier, including questions that need git implicitly (whether a file is tracked or ignored, history); no explorer, mechanic or engineer node is asked to answer them

checklist.name: Git nodes are standalone
checklist.description: No single node mixes git/gh/glab commands with non-git work; any node needing both is split into separate nodes

checklist.name: Tiers follow the skill's rule
checklist.description: Each node's tier follows the skill's order: Git if it runs git, Easy if every edit and command is literal, Medium if the target is fully specified, otherwise Hard. Where a contract is open, a Hard node (a design node or the build node) settles it; code that must keep a silent-failure invariant is Hard unless its acceptance includes a test that fails when the invariant breaks; no reviewer is below Hard without a written reason

checklist.name: Required inspections planned
checklist.description: Every Hard build node, and every Medium build node whose acceptance includes a command, has a separate inspector node that depends on it, and the plan states the build node is accepted only after the inspector passes. Git, review, discovery, design and verify nodes have no inspector

checklist.name: Inspector uses Easy or Haiku
checklist.description: The inspector nodes are Easy tier or the Haiku model, not Medium or Hard

checklist.name: Inspector gets no implementer material
checklist.description: The inspector nodes are not sent the build order's Changes, the implementer's report or claimed results, or the mister's diagnosis or suggested fix

checklist.name: Log without fabricated state
checklist.description: plan.md has a Log section. Because the plan was only approved, it holds no transition line (dispatched, done, failed, superseded), at most a note line starting with '- '; no node is planned to receive a done line without being dispatched

checklist.name: Log lines are single sentences
checklist.description: Every Log line is a single readable sentence of ordinary prose on one line, not a multi-line block, nested list or code block

checklist.name: No state outside the Log
checklist.description: Node blocks carry no status or state field, and no other section of plan.md says what is running, done or next. Header fields the plan template allows to read `pending, <node id>` (Starting HEAD, Task base SHA) do not count

checklist.name: Parallel readiness
checklist.description: The DAG has at least one point where two or more nodes with disjoint owns and no shared contract become ready on the same dependencies, while worktree-rewriting Git nodes run alone

checklist.name: Baseline checks before build work
checklist.description: Before any build node, a node records SHA-256 digests of the protected untracked paths and runs the repository's test command on the task base into a capture, so later failures can be told apart from pre-existing ones

checklist.name: Real paths in owns
checklist.description: Every owns list names real paths only: no placeholders such as '(pending N0x)' and no either-or alternatives

checklist.name: Plan location and command directories
checklist.description: plan.md is written at ./the-mister/add-user-activity/plan.md and records the git dir /work/user-service/.git in its header. Every command starts with cd /work/user-service && or git -C /work/user-service, or uses only absolute paths; paths taken from git output are made absolute
